newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Turkish workers can stay in EU without job-court.
newsitem.headline: Turkish workers can stay in EU without job-court.

text.p: The European Court of Justice ruled on Thursday that longtime Turkish "guest" workers can stay on in European Union countries for a time even if they have lost their jobs.

It said that under the terms of an agreement between the EU and Ankara, Turkish workers employed in a member state for at least four years may remain in residence for a reasonable period, even if unemployed, to seek a new job.
The court said the reasonable period should be fixed by national law but must be long enough for a worker to have a fair chance to secure new employment.
In the case in question, a Turkish national was employed on various German ships and obtained successive resident permits between 1980 and 1988.
In 1988, he moved to Berlin and sought an unlimited residence permit while seeking new employment. He was denied this by a local court, based on German law.
The EU court said that a longstanding EU-Turkey Association agreement took precedence. It added, however, that to be covered the workers had to comply with local employment rules.
